note: WORKTREE-TAKE RECYCLES A CAMPAIGN THAT HAS NOT STARTED YET, and this is very likely why handoff notes keep vanishing. The recycle test in scripts/worktree-take.sh lines 82-110 is two conditions: the tree is clean modulo docs/timings/test-baseline-, AND merge-base --is-ancestor branch origin/main. A BRAND-NEW CAMPAIGN BRANCH SATISFIES BOTH -- clean because nothing is committed yet, and trivially an ancestor because it IS mains tip. So a freshly taken worktree is eligible for recycling by the very next caller until its first commit. For a spec-first campaign that window spans the entire brainstorm, and worktree-take sweeps .superpowers/sdd/ on recycle by design, so the decision ledger and any handoff note go with it. The guards own comment anticipates the opposite end of the lifecycle: a session mid-cleanup after its own merge has a merged branch and live uncommitted work. That covers a campaign that FINISHED, not one that has not STARTED. OBSERVED THREE TIMES ON 2026-08-20 in one session: the-bridle recycled into the-cupel mid-conversation, then a replacement the-deed recycled within minutes, twice. SECOND-ORDER TRAP: recycling orphans the branch, and worktree-take then REFUSES to re-take the same name with a branch already exists fatal. Recovery is git worktree add PATH EXISTING-BRANCH, not another worktree-take. MITIGATION THAT NEEDS NO RULE CHANGE: the scripts own awk filter already skips locked worktrees, so run git worktree lock on the worktree immediately after taking it and unlock at close. Verified by running that same awk over live git worktree list --porcelain output and confirming the locked worktree is absent from the candidate set, rather than by reading the filter. Committing anything to the branch also closes the window, since the branch stops being an ancestor of main. PROPER FIX for whoever owns the pool: lock on take inside worktree-take.sh, and make the liveness test distinguish never-started from finished.
